chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: First professional recording for the Bihari brothers
summary: The Modern Records session with McGhee, 'Deep Meditation', in which he echoed Coleman Hawkins.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But before we get too far, I'd like to go back a little ways and talk about my first professional recording. It was with Howard McGhee's group, the original group, and we did a recording for a little record store back behind the Civic Hotel, where I was living at the time. They started their own record label. They were doing the little pressing; they had one pressing machine -- they were doing a whole one-man
production from the record store. And it was called Modern Records at the time. The Bihari Brothers, Jules, Joe and Sol. They had this little record store, and decided to go into the record thing.

And the first thing that we recorded was a thing called "Deep Meditation" with Howard McGhee. I actually was trying to emulate Coleman Hawkins to a degree, because he had just finished working with Hawkins, and he had told me about how this song...he could imagine Hawk doing it, you know. So I tried to emulate Coleman Hawkins to a degree on "Deep Meditation." In fact, that's about the only time I ever tried to do somebody else on a record. Except one time later on when I did a movie soundtrack, and the setting was 1932, and I did it with Chu Berry, the tenor player, in mind -- Leon "Chu" Berry.
